rows.title: [BUG] AI Gateway streaming passthrough calls made via plain REST (no MLflow SDK client) never get mlflow.chat.tokenUsage attached, so trace-level Tokens/Cost stay empty
rows.excerpt:
n consumed, calls `_set_span_token_usage()` → `mlflow.get_current_active_span()` to attach `CHAT_USAGE`. That depends on the tracing contextvar staying correctly scoped for the *entire* lifetime of an async generator driven by Starlette's `StreamingResponse` — i.e. well after the route handler that opened the span has already returned control to the ASGI server.

Notably, `mlflow/server/fastapi_app.py` already has a comment acknowledging this exact class of behavior for streaming responses:

```python
# Reset the ContextVar so the handler task starts at 0. The handler task
# inherits a copy of this context (Starlette's call_next uses copy_context),
# so the reset is visible to send_request inside the handler.
...
# For non-streaming responses, duration_ms covers the full round-trip.
# For streaming responses, duration_ms covers only gateway setup time
# (until the StreamingResponse object is returned, before the stream body
# is iterated), so it reflects time-to-first-stream rather than total
# streaming duration.
# We can't read the ContextVar directly here because the handler runs in a
# separate task and ContextVar mutations don't propagate back.
```

We tried to reproduce this in isolation to narrow it down further — three variants, including one that mirrors `mlflow.gateway.tracing_utils.maybe_traced_gateway_call`'s actual wiring almost line-for-line (`mlflow.trace()` decorator around an async-gen wrapper, `output_reducer`, an explicit `trace_destination=MlflowExperimentLocation(...)`, `provider.passthrough()` nested inside it). **All three worked correctly** — `mlflow.chat.tokenUsage` attached fine every time (see repro script below). So whatever breaks context propagation in our real deployment is something a synthetic, instantly-yielding local generator doesn't trigger — most likely something about real network streaming timing through the actual provider HTTP client, or ASGI-level concurrency under real request load, that only shows up under production conditions.

We're actively trying to pin down the exact trigger with a temporary diagnostic (logging `mlflow.get_current_active_span()` at stream-start vs. stream-end in our own build) and will report back what we find, but wanted to file this now given how broadly it affects gateway users who don't use the MLflow SDK client.

rows.title: [BUG] Budget policy refresh deletes every other workspace's budget window
rows.excerpt:
d against is global. Every refresh therefore treats every other workspace's policies as stale and deletes their window and policy keys.

**Expected:** a refresh triggered by traffic in workspace A leaves workspace B's tracked window
alone.

**Actual:** workspace B's window is deleted. Only the most recently refreshed workspace has a tracked window at any moment, so a `REJECT` policy in any other workspace cannot be evaluated - `should_reject_request` iterates the policy set, finds nothing for that workspace, and returns `(False, None)`.

Observed on a server with six workspace-scoped policies in `budget_policies`:

```
mlflow:budget:policies → 1 member
  bp-25c0ffff…  my-budget  10000.0  1:DAYS  REJECT
```

The other five workspaces had no window. Which workspace survives is simply whichever refreshed most recently, so the set changes hands as traffic moves between workspaces.

Both the spend and the `exceeded` flag do come back once the owning workspace refreshes again: the recreated window is returned as fresh, and `backfill_spend` re-derives spend from trace history and recomputes `exceeded` from it. The damage is the gap in between, and the gap is not short. A wipe also calls `mark_refreshed()`, so the owning workspace will not refresh again until `MLFLOW_GATEWAY_BUDGET_REFRESH_INTERVAL` (default 600s) has elapsed. On a server taking traffic in several workspaces the wipes keep alternating, so all but the most recently refreshed workspace sit unenforced more or less permanently.

A second effect: after a wipe the next recorded cost flips `exceeded` from 0 to 1 again, so an `ALERT` policy fires its webhook a second time for the same window. That is the opposite failure to #26054, from the same lost flag.

rows.title: [FR] Make the experiment run Columns selector resizable
rows.excerpt:
crolling. Long column names are also truncated, requiring users to hover over individual entries to determine their full names. This is particularly noticeable on large, ultrawide, and high-resolution displays where significantly more screen space is available but cannot be used by the selector.

I propose allowing users to resize the Columns selector horizontally and vertically on desktop.

Proposed behavior:

- Preserve approximately the current dimensions as the initial/default size.
- Allow the panel to be resized horizontally and vertically.
- Constrain resizing to the available viewport/popover area.
- Keep the column tree scrollable within the resized panel.
- Preserve the existing mobile/full-width behavior and disable manual resizing on small screens.
- Preserve existing search, keyboard navigation, column selection, and **Reset to defaults** behavior.

This would be a frontend-only enhancement to `ExperimentViewRunsColumnSelector` and would not require changes to experiment data or MLflow APIs.

A previous MLflow change, https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/pull/2388, addressed aggressive truncation in this selector by increasing its width and improving hover behavior. Allowing user-controlled sizing would avoid requiring another globally fixed size while adapting better to different display sizes and experiment configurations.

I am willing to contribute the implementation.

### Motivation

#### What is the use case for this feature?

When analyzing experiments with a large number of parameters and metrics, users frequently need to enable and disable columns in the experiment runs table.

For larger experiments, the list in the **Columns** selector can contain dozens or hundreds of entries. Many parameter and metric names can also be relatively long, particularly when configuration values are represented using hierarchical names such as:

`synthetic_augmentation.generator.candidate_location...`

The current selector provides a relatively small fixed viewing area regardless of the available screen space. As a result, users must scroll through a small portion of the available column list and often hover over truncated entries to determine their complete names.

Allowing the panel to be resized would let users temporarily expand the selector while configuring their experiment table and then return to the normal interface afterward.
